metadata.disclaimer: These ranges are based on publicly available data and are intended for illustrative purposes only. Actual deal terms vary significantly based on asset-specific factors, market conditions, and negotiation dynamics.
metadata.marketNotes: 2026 values reflect continued strength in oncology licensing, with radiopharmaceutical and ADC deals driving premiums. Neurology/CNS calibrated against 88 R&D partnerships totaling $45.9B. Immunology/Autoimmune added as third therapeutic area — the second-largest biopharma deal market ($246B projected by 2032) with 33 partnerships worth $13B in 2024 alone. CAR-T for autoimmune, anti-TL1A, and FcRn antagonists driving paradigm shifts. Metabolic/Obesity added as fourth therapeutic area — the fastest-growing pharma segment ($100B+ obesity market projected by 2030) with GLP-1, dual/triple incretin, and oral peptide deals driving unprecedented valuations.

sglt2Inhibitor+ckdMetabolic.context: SGLT2 validated in CKD (DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY); renal protection beyond glycemic control

glp1Agonist+hfpef.context: GLP-1 showing HFpEF benefit via weight loss and metabolic improvement; SELECT trial

rnai+familialHypercholesterolemia.context: siRNA inclisiran validated for FH; Novartis franchise; PCSK9 silencing paradigm

neurologyDiseaseModifyingPhaseAdjustment._description: Disease-modifying neurology assets have longer development timelines. These multipliers adjust milestone allocations to weight development milestones higher.

tooltips: Radiopharmaceuticals commanding 50-60% premiums after Novartis/Point ($4.9B) and BMS/RayzeBio ($4.1B) acquisitions
ADCs remain hot - Merck, Pfizer, others actively acquiring
IRA creating pressure on ex-US deal values, especially EU-only rights
China rights increasingly carved out or discounted due to geopolitical/regulatory uncertainty
Phase 2 assets with breakthrough designation seeing 2024 upfronts 20%+ above 2023

modality.radiopharmaceutical: Radiopharmaceuticals are commanding 50-60% premiums in 2025. Leverage the Point/RayzeBio deals as comparables.
modality.adc: ADCs remain highly sought after. Push for higher upfront given Merck, Pfizer acquisition activity.
modality.bispecific: Bispecific T-cell engagers are accelerating. Highlight differentiated safety/efficacy profile.
modality.protac: PROTAC/degrader deals continue strong. Emphasize oral bioavailability and target coverage.
modality.molecularGlue: Molecular glues are a hot emerging category. Novel targets can command premium.
modality.geneTherapy: Gene therapy valuations cooling due to manufacturing/durability concerns. Expect scrutiny on CMC.
modality.carT_heme: CAR-T in heme is maturing. Manufacturing cost and vein-to-vein time are key negotiation points.

lineOfTherapy.1L: First-line potential significantly increases value. Emphasize 1L pathway and unmet need in discussions.
lineOfTherapy.3L+: Third-line+ positioning limits peak sales potential. Consider demonstrating combo or earlier-line potential.

competitivePosition.firstInClass: First-in-class mechanism provides significant leverage. Emphasize novel biology and lack of alternatives.
competitivePosition.crowded: Crowded competitive space - expect pushback on royalties. Consider flexibility on milestones.
competitivePosition.behind: Behind competitors - focus on differentiation (safety, convenience, combo potential) to justify terms.

territory.china: China rights increasingly carved out due to geopolitical uncertainty. Consider geographic splits.
territory.europe: IRA creating pressure on EU-only value. US rights are key driver - consider split deals.

dataQuality.pivotalReady: Pivotal-ready data significantly de-risks the asset. Push for premium upfront.
dataQuality.limited: Limited data increases risk profile. Expect milestone-heavy structure with lower upfront.

regulatory.breakthrough: Breakthrough designation adds credibility and expedited pathway. Use as negotiation leverage.

neurologyModality.bbbPlatform: BBB delivery platforms command 2-3x premiums due to multi-program optionality. Leverage AZ/JCR ($825M) and ABL/GSK ($2.7B) as comparables.
neurologyModality.aso: ASOs have a proven regulatory path in neuro (Spinraza precedent). Emphasize genetic target validation and manufacturing scalability.
neurologyModality.psychedelic: Psychedelic/neuroplastogen deals are nascent but high-value. AbbVie/Gilgamesh ($1.2B) sets the benchmark for differentiated Phase 2 assets.
neurologyModality.geneTherapy: CNS gene therapy commands higher premiums than oncology gene therapy due to curative potential for monogenic disorders. Expect scrutiny on BBB penetration and durability.
neurologyModality.ionChannel: Ion channel modulators are gaining traction in epilepsy and pain. Nav1.8 (Vertex precedent) and genetic epilepsy channels command differentiated terms. Emphasize selectivity data.
neurologyModality.tauTargeting: Tau-targeting therapies are the next wave after amyloid validation. Tau PET-guided patient selection and disease modification data are key negotiation leverage points.
neurologyModality.stemCell: Neural stem cell/progenitor therapies command premiums for curative potential. BlueRock/Bayer ($1B+) sets the benchmark. CMC and scalability are critical discussion points.

neurologyIndication.alzheimers: Alzheimer's commands the highest CNS premiums. Anti-amyloid approvals validated the space. BBB-crossing assets at significant premium.
neurologyIndication.schizophrenia: Schizophrenia deals reset by KarXT/Cobenfy approval. Novel mechanisms (muscarinic agonists) commanding premium over D2-based approaches.
neurologyIndication.als: ALS carries maximum orphan premiums with critical unmet need. ASO/gene therapy approaches lead. Biogen/Ionis tofersen (SOD1) validates genetic targeting in ALS.
neurologyIndication.huntingtons: Huntington's is a validated genetic target with orphan premiums. Novartis/PTC $1B upfront sets the benchmark. Allele-selective silencing commands premium.
neurologyIndication.narcolepsy: Narcolepsy is an orphan-adjacent market dominated by Jazz and Harmony. Orexin biology expanding. Novel mechanisms can command premium for differentiation.
neurologyIndication.epilepsy: Epilepsy gene therapy and ion channel approaches attract orphan premiums for rare epilepsy syndromes. Broad epilepsy is competitive — differentiate on mechanism.
neurologyIndication.tbi: TBI/stroke recovery has zero approved disease-modifying treatments. Massive unmet need but regulatory path uncertain. Neuroprotection/regeneration data is key.
neurologyIndication.depression: MDD is a large but competitive market. Differentiation (novel MOA, rapid onset, reduced side effects) is critical for premium terms.
neurologyIndication.rareNeuro: Rare neurological diseases carry orphan drug premiums. Gene therapy and ASO approaches for monogenic CNS disorders can command curative-potential premiums.
neurologyIndication.bipolar: Bipolar disorder has a large underserved population. CAPLYTA expansion and lithium-sparing approaches are driving renewed pharma interest. Novel MOAs command premium.
neurologyIndication.ptsd: PTSD is gaining traction with psychedelic-assisted therapy approaches. High unmet need and growing societal awareness. Regulatory pathway still evolving.
neurologyIndication.ocd: OCD has limited approved options beyond SSRIs. Psilocybin and glutamate modulation are emerging. Differentiated mechanisms command premium for treatment-resistant patients.
neurologyIndication.autism: Autism spectrum disorder has zero approved disease-modifying treatments. Massive underserved population creates enormous TAM potential. Genetic subtype targeting (Fragile X, Rett) carries orphan premiums.
neurologyIndication.rett: Rett syndrome was validated by Acadia's trofinetide approval. Gene therapy approaches (MECP2 replacement) command curative-potential premiums. Orphan designation ensures market exclusivity.
neurologyIndication.friedreichs: Friedreich's ataxia is a genetically validated orphan indication. Frataxin gene therapy approaches advancing. Biogen and Lexeo are active. Premium terms for disease modification.
neurologyIndication.dmd: Duchenne muscular dystrophy commands the highest premiums in pediatric neuromuscular. Gene therapy (Sarepta's Elevidys) established the paradigm. Micro-dystrophin and exon-skipping approaches both active.
neurologyIndication.chronicPain: Non-neuropathic chronic pain is a large market but regulatory-complex post-opioid crisis. Nav1.7/Nav1.8 and non-opioid approaches are the focus. Expect rigorous safety requirements.

treatmentApproach.diseaseModifying: Disease-modifying status significantly increases value in neurodegeneration. Emphasize biomarker evidence of disease modification in negotiations.
treatmentApproach.adjunctive: Adjunctive positioning limits standalone commercial potential. Consider demonstrating disease-modifying potential or earlier-line data.

immunologyModality.carT_autoimmune: CAR-T for autoimmune is the hottest modality in biopharma. Leverage Kyverna's regulatory path and dramatic DORIS remission data. Curative potential commands massive premiums.
immunologyModality.inVivoCarT: In vivo CAR-T eliminates apheresis and manufacturing bottlenecks. AbbVie/Capstan $2.1B validates the approach. Emphasize scalability and cost-of-goods advantage.
immunologyModality.carTreg: CAR-Treg represents antigen-specific tolerance without immunosuppression. Still early-stage; emphasize differentiation from broad immunosuppression approaches.
immunologyModality.fcrnAntagonist: FcRn antagonists are a validated platform (Vyvgart $3B+ revenue). J&J/Momenta $6.5B sets the benchmark. Highlight multi-indication expansion potential.
immunologyModality.complementInhibitor: Complement inhibitors have AZ/Alexion's $39B franchise as precedent. Oral complement is the next wave. Emphasize differentiation from Soliris/Ultomiris.
immunologyModality.tl1aInhibitor: Anti-TL1A is the hottest target class in autoimmune. Merck/Prometheus $10.8B and Roche/Telavant $7.1B reset market expectations entirely.
immunologyModality.oralIntegrin: Oral integrin inhibitors represent the oral vedolizumab thesis. Lilly/Morphic $3.2B acquisition validates. Emphasize oral convenience advantage.
immunologyModality.dualAntagonist: BAFF/APRIL dual antagonists are validated by Vertex/Alpine $4.9B. IgAN and lupus nephritis applications carry premium. Multi-mechanism MOA is the differentiator.

immunologyIndication.sle_lupus: SLE is being transformed by CAR-T showing drug-free remissions. Belimumab was the only targeted therapy for decades. Novel approaches command massive premiums.
immunologyIndication.crohns: Crohn's Disease is the premier anti-TL1A indication. Merck/Prometheus $10.8B deal validates. Oral approaches and fibrosis reduction are key differentiators.
immunologyIndication.ulcerativeColitis: UC has multiple competing mechanisms (S1P, JAK, TL1A, integrin) but remains high-value. Oral convenience is a major differentiator over biologics.
immunologyIndication.myastheniaGravis: MG was transformed by FcRn antagonists (Vyvgart). Complement and CAR-T approaches expanding. High unmet need in refractory patients.
immunologyIndication.igan: IgA Nephropathy validated by Vertex/Alpine $4.9B acquisition. BAFF/APRIL mechanism established. Complement and endothelin approaches expanding.
immunologyIndication.pnh: PNH is the cornerstone complement indication. AZ/Alexion franchise ($6B+ revenue). Oral C5 and next-gen complement targets are the frontier.
immunologyIndication.rareAutoimmune: Rare autoimmune conditions carry orphan drug premiums. Myositis, stiff-person syndrome — all attracting CAR-T and novel biologic approaches.
immunologyIndication.celiac: Celiac disease has zero approved therapies — patients rely entirely on dietary gluten avoidance. Massive underserved population (~1% prevalence). Multiple Phase 2 programs active.
immunologyIndication.vitiligo: Vitiligo was validated by ruxolitinib cream approval. JAK inhibitors dominate but novel approaches (melanocyte stimulation, immune modulation) can differentiate. Moderate deal sizes.
immunologyIndication.pemphigus: Pemphigus/bullous diseases have high unmet need despite rituximab. CAR-T showing dramatic B-cell depletion and skin clearance. Orphan premiums for severe autoimmune blistering.
immunologyIndication.itp: ITP is expanding beyond TPO agonists. FcRn antagonists validated the IgG-reduction approach. Complement and novel biologics pipeline growing. Multi-indication expansion potential.
immunologyIndication.asthma: Severe asthma biologics are a $10B+ market. TSLP (tezepelumab), IL-33, and anti-alarmin approaches expanding. Differentiation from anti-IL5 and anti-IL4/13 is key for premium terms.
immunologyIndication.eosinophilicEsophagitis: EoE was transformed by dupilumab approval. High unmet need with limited approved options. Anti-IL-13, TSLP, and small molecule approaches in pipeline. Premium for oral delivery.
immunologyIndication.gvhd: GVHD carries orphan premiums with high mortality in severe cases. JAK inhibitors (ruxolitinib, belumosudil) approved. CAR-Treg and tolerizing approaches are the next frontier.
immunologyIndication.organTransplant: Solid organ transplant rejection has massive unmet need for calcineurin-free regimens. Kidney injury and chronic rejection drive long-term costs. Tegoprubart and costimulation blockade gaining traction.
immunologyIndication.thyroidEye: Thyroid eye disease was validated by Tepezza ($2B+ peak sales). IGF-1R targeting established. Expansion to moderate disease and novel targets (FcRn, complement) attracting deal interest.
immunologyIndication.pbc: Primary biliary cholangitis expanded with elafibranor approval. PPAR agonists validated. Orphan-adjacent with growing pipeline interest. Combination approaches for inadequate responders.

immuneResetPotential.curativeIntent: Curative intent (drug-free remission) is the holy grail in autoimmune. CAR-T and tolerizing approaches command 40%+ premiums. Emphasize DORIS remission data.
immuneResetPotential.chronicTreatment: Chronic treatment models have predictable recurring revenue but face biosimilar/generic pressure. Differentiation and adherence advantages are key.

targetSpecificity.antigenSpecific: Antigen-specific approaches (CAR-Treg, tolerizing) avoid broad immunosuppression. This is the next frontier — emphasize safety advantage over broad immunosuppressants.
targetSpecificity.broadImmunosuppression: Broad immunosuppression faces commoditization pressure. Infection risk concerns limit use in milder disease. Focus on rapid onset and bridge-to-maintenance positioning.

metabolicModality.glp1Agonist: GLP-1 agonists dominate metabolic. Semaglutide is the fastest-growing drug in history. Differentiation via oral delivery, superior efficacy, or muscle-sparing profiles is essential for premium terms.
metabolicModality.dualIncretin: Dual incretins represent the next wave after mono-GLP-1. Tirzepatide's superior efficacy data validates the approach. Emphasize comparative weight loss and CV outcome data.
metabolicModality.tripleIncretin: Triple agonists (GLP-1/GIP/glucagon) represent the frontier. Retatrutide's 24% weight loss is category-leading. Early-stage but commanding maximum interest.
metabolicModality.oralPeptide: Oral metabolic peptides are the holy grail. Oral semaglutide proved the concept ($2B+ revenue). Next-gen oral formulations with bioavailability improvements command massive premiums.
metabolicModality.antiActivin: Anti-activin/myostatin approaches differentiate by preserving lean mass during weight loss. Emphasize body composition data vs. GLP-1 muscle loss.
metabolicModality.microbiomeBased: Microbiome-based metabolic therapies are emerging but unvalidated. Expect milestone-heavy structures with proof-of-concept gates.

metabolicIndication.obesity: Obesity is the single largest commercial opportunity in pharma history ($100B+ projected). Competition from Novo and Lilly is intense. Differentiation via oral delivery, superior efficacy, or muscle-sparing is critical.
metabolicIndication.nashMash: NASH/MASH was validated by resmetirom approval. GLP-1 data in MASH is transformative. Multi-mechanism approaches are attracting platform deal interest.
metabolicIndication.type2Diabetes: T2D is the largest established metabolic market but increasingly commoditized. Differentiation via oral delivery, fewer GI side effects, or CV/renal benefit is essential.
metabolicIndication.rareMetabolic: Rare metabolic disorders carry orphan drug premiums. Gene therapy and enzyme replacement approaches for monogenic conditions command curative-potential premiums.
metabolicIndication.type1Diabetes: Type 1 diabetes is being transformed. Teplizumab delays onset (first disease-modifying approval). Cell therapy (islet replacement, immune evasion capsules) commands curative premiums. Massive long-term market.
metabolicIndication.ckdMetabolic: CKD in the metabolic context is validated by SGLT2 data (DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY) and finerenone. GLP-1 agonists showing CKD benefit. Cardio-renal-metabolic nexus deals command multi-indication premiums.
metabolicIndication.hfpef: HFpEF is the largest unmet need in cardiology. SGLT2 (empagliflozin, dapagliflozin) validated. GLP-1 and metabolic approaches showing benefit. Premium for cardiometabolic dual-indication data.
metabolicIndication.familialHypercholesterolemia: Familial hypercholesterolemia is an orphan indication with validated targets. PCSK9 (mAb and siRNA), ANGPTL3, and Lp(a) approaches all attracting deals. Premium for severe/homozygous FH.
metabolicIndication.gout: Gout is a large market but dominated by generics (allopurinol, febuxostat). Premium terms require differentiation — biologics for refractory (pegloticase), IL-1 inhibition, or novel urate-lowering mechanisms.
metabolicIndication.wilsonDisease: Wilson disease is a high-unmet-need orphan condition. Current chelation therapy is poorly tolerated. Gene therapy (ATP7B replacement) commands curative premiums. Very few competitors.
metabolicIndication.fabry: Fabry disease has established ERT ($2B+ market) but gene therapy commands significant premium for one-time curative potential. 4D Molecular, Freeline, and others advancing. Replacement of chronic ERT is the thesis.
metabolicIndication.gaucher: Gaucher disease pioneered enzyme replacement therapy. Gene therapy and substrate reduction approaches offer next-gen potential. Sanofi franchise ($1B+) established. Premium for durability over ERT.

mechanismDifferentiation.nonIncretin: Non-incretin mechanisms command premium for differentiation from the GLP-1 duopoly. Emphasize complementary biology, muscle-sparing, or central satiety pathways.
mechanismDifferentiation.combinationMechanism: Multi-pathway mechanisms are the frontier. Triple agonists, GLP-1 + amylin combos, and metabolic + anti-inflammatory approaches show the highest efficacy.

routeOfAdministration.oral: Oral administration is the single biggest competitive differentiator in metabolic. Patient preference, primary care prescribing, and payer formulary access all favor oral. Premium of 20-30% over injectable equivalents.
routeOfAdministration.implantable: Long-acting implantable/depot formulations address adherence. Monthly or less frequent dosing eliminates injection burden. Emerging category.
